text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT P1 — Billing ingestion delayed: downstream metering consumers reporting 30–60m lag for ingestion window. Paging on-call (matt_oncall) and billing team. Severity: potential customer overage flags. Runbook: billing-ingest -> ‘ingest-delay’. 

matt_oncall: I'm paged, looking now. Can someone confirm which pipeline (ingest/kafka/transform) first observed delays?

sara_billing: Observed alert from usage-recon job at 12:04 UTC reporting >45m behind. Verified sample invoices showing missing window for 11:00-11:30. Likely ingest or kafka consumer lag. :frowning:

tj_dataeng: Checking kafka offsets for topic billing-raw-usw2. Quick check:

```
$ KAFKA_OFFSETS=bin/kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka01:9092 --describe --group billing-ingest-consumer
TOPIC                PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG             CONSUMER-ID
billing-raw-usw2     0          123456789       123456889       100             consumer-7
billing-raw-usw2     1          123333000       123333050       50
```

tj_dataeng: There's consistent lag on partition 0 (~100 records) but that doesn't explain 45m. Looking at consumer commit times — last commit around 11:15 UTC, nothing since.

matt_oncall: Any recent deploys to billing-ingest? Did the autoscaler evict pods in the kube node pool?

ops-jen: I see a node replacement event at 11:22 UTC tied to a maintenance window for nodepool-west. kube events show billing-ingest-0 restarted and backoff events for a minute.

sara_billing: That explains consumer pause, but post-restart consumer should catch up. Why hasn't it processed >40m backlog? Check if consumer group is stuck or schema mismatch.

tj_dataeng: Looking at logs (tail):

```
2026-03-15T11:23:05Z ERROR consumer-WORKER java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unknown schema version v3.2 for message
2026-03-15T11:23:05Z ERROR consumer-WORKER Failed to deserialize record, skipping
2026-03-15T11:24:10Z WARN  consumer-WORKER Too many deserialization failures, pausing consumption
```

tj_dataeng: A producer rolled to new schema v3.2 at 11:22 (hotfix) but consumers haven't been updated — they pause on unknown schema to avoid bad ingests. That would block processing and cause delayed usage metrics.

devon_product: Which customers are affected? Any billing overage flags or emails already triggered?

lina_csm: I have two CSMs reporting customer complaints about delayed invoices and one customer saw pre-emptive overage warning from the dashboard (usage > quota flag) — likely due to stale reconciliation. Customer is AcmeCorp (contacted us). They want ETA.

matt_oncall: OK. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll back producer schema change, 2) Update consumers to accept v3.2, 3) Temporary allow-deserialize-fallback in consumer to skip unknown fields. Which is fastest?

sara_billing: Shortest path is rollback on producers (coord with whoever deployed). But rollout might be ongoing across regions. Quick fallback: enable permissive-deserialize flag (we have feature flag) to treat unknown schema versions as best-effort — will keep counts but may lose some new fields. I'll prepare the flag toggle.

ops-jen: Preparing toggle: patch configmap billing-consumer-config -> set permissive_deserialize=true. Applying to namespace-prod-usw2 now.

```
kubectl -n prod patch cm billing-consumer-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/permissive_deserialize","value":"true"}]'
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment billing-ingest
```

ops-jen: Patch applied, rollout triggered. Restarting consumers.

matt_oncall: Watching consumer logs and offsets.

tj_dataeng: After restart — consumers pick up at 11:30 and begin processing backlog. Offsets catching up. Estimated catch-up rate ~20k msgs/min. With backlog ~600k, ETA ~30 minutes. :thumbsup:

sara_billing: Can we confirm token counting integrity? If permissive mode strips some optional fields, token counts should still be computed, but need to validate sample hashes.

tj_dataeng: Running sample reconciliation job between raw ingest and metered counts for a 10-minute slice:

```
SELECT count(1) as raw_msgs, sum(token_count) as tokens_raw
FROM billing.raw_messages
WHERE partition_ts >= '2026-03-15T11:00:00Z' AND partition_ts < '2026-03-15T11:10:00Z';

SELECT count(1) as meter_msgs, sum(tokens) as tokens_meter
FROM billing.metered_usage
WHERE window_start >= '2026-03-15T11:00:00Z' AND window_start < '2026-03-15T11:10:00Z';
```

tj_dataeng: Preliminary: raw_msgs 120k, tokens_raw 3.2M; meter_msgs 118k, tokens_meter 3.18M. Diff within expected recon variance. Looks good so far.

lina_csm: Can we message AcmeCorp with an ETA? They asked to avoid alarms. Suggest: "We identified an ingestion schema mismatch causing delayed billing updates; we've applied a temporary tolerance and ingestion is catching up, expected reconciliation complete in ~45 minutes. No billing overcharges will be applied retroactively." Need Ops/legal confirmation.

devon_product: Draft looks good. Ops/legal: can we guarantee no automatic overage charges during this incident window? We usually freeze alerts for known ingestion delays.

matt_oncall: I'm going to create a short mitigation note and open a billing freeze on the overage alert pipeline.

sara_billing: Creating billing-freeze flag in alerts config -> set mute for rule overage-warning-prod for window 11:20-13:00 UTC.

ops-jen: Mute applied.

tj_dataeng: Offsets fully caught up at 12:02 UTC, reconciliation job run. Final counts show 0.6% message loss in one micro-partition due to deserialization failures earlier (handled by skip policy) — devices affected are <0.1% of customers. We'll run backfill for those messages if available in dead-letter-store.

sara_billing: Noted. Start backfill job: reprocess from the DLQ for topic billing-raw-usw2 partition 0 from offset 123456789 to 123456889.

```
# backfill script
python tools/replay_kafka.py --topic billing-raw-usw2 --partition 0 --from 123456789 --to 123456889 --consumer-mode=reprocess
```

tj_dataeng: Backfill started at 12:10 UTC. Should finish ~15m. After that, run final reconciliation to ensure token counts match and generate note for finance.

lina_csm: I'll update AcmeCorp with: ETA ~30–45 minutes, we will not bill for any spurious overage alerts and will follow up with confirmation when reconciliation completes. Send me the note before sending.

matt_oncall: Great. Next steps: 1) Wait for backfill + reconciliation, 2) Confirm token counts match production windows, 3) Unmute alerts once safe, 4) Post-incident RCA — cause: producer schema rollout without coordinated consumer compatibility check; remediation: stricter schema gating + automated consumer canary. Assignments: sara_billing lead on RCA, tj_dataeng on backfill, matt_oncall on incident postmortem doc.

devon_product: Also propose a new policy: require schema compatibility flag in CI for producers. Add to backlog.

sara_billing: I've captured tasks in the incident board and assigned owners.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigated (ingest resumed, backfill in progress). Next update scheduled in 20 minutes or on completion.

lina_csm: Thanks all. I'll hold off on notifying customers until we have final reconciliation. :relieved:

matt_oncall: Thanks team. I'll start the postmortem doc and include timelines, mitigations, and follow-ups. Closing thread when reconciliation passes.

ops-jen: Backfill complete at 12:22 UTC, reconciliation pass ran at 12:25 UTC. Final diff within 0.02% — no billing adjustments needed. Unmuting alerts now.

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — incident closed at 12:30 UTC. Root cause: breaking schema change on producer during maintenance. Follow-ups scheduled.

matt_oncall: Closing thread. Postmortem draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1323 (assigns: sara, tj, devops)
